groups.label: Decide whether a relation is a function

statements.text: A relation from X to Y is said to be a function if each of the elements of X appears only once as a first projection in one of the ordered pairs of the relation.

The function is denoted by one of the symbols f or m or Q, etc. The function f from the set X to the set Y is written mathematically as f : X → Y and is read as "f is a function from X to Y". Formula: $f : X \rightarrow Y$
If f is a function from X to itself, we say that f is a function on X.

If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, then the element y is called the image of the element x by the function f, and we express it in one of two forms: f : x ↦ y, read as "the function f maps x to y"; or f(x) = y, read as "f is a function where f(x) = y". Formula: $f : x \mapsto y$, $f(x) = y$

groups.label: Find the domain, codomain and range of a function

statements.text: The set X is called the domain of the function f.
The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.
The set of images of the elements of the domain X by the function f is called the range of the function.
The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.
